local: H1 and H2: this machine’s saved Gemini CLI sessions, counts only

verdicts.claim: Import is faithful on real sessions: for every Gemini CLI session saved on this machine, the imported record holds exactly the session's tool calls (each distinct tool-call id, in the order first written, by name) and one model call per distinct Gemini reply, as counted by a separate reading of the raw lines; and every imported record fits the strict schema (P0 passes).
verdicts.measured: 3 real sessions: 3 imported faithfully (4 tool uses for 4 tool calls read separately; 6 model calls for 6 replies); 3 fit the strict schema

verdicts.claim: A past session is never dressed up: every imported real session, having no sealed intent, fails P1, and its intent's goal says none was sealed.
verdicts.measured: 3 real sessions: P1 failed on 2; the intent says none was sealed on 3

verdicts.claim: The format as found: for 500 seeded synthetic sessions in that format (a header, $set lines, user and Gemini messages, replies written again with their tool calls, and a $set of messages that replaces the list), the import gives exactly the events the generator meant, in order: one model call per reply with its model and time, then one tool use per tool call with its name and time.
verdicts.measured: 500 of 500 synthetic sessions imported to exactly the 3811 events meant (157 of them with a list of messages replaced)

verdicts.claim: Total: 2,000 garbage inputs (lines that are not JSON or not an object, lines of the wrong shape or with fields of the wrong type, and synthetic sessions cut at a random point) never make the importer throw; each line that is not a JSON object is counted as unreadable; and the strict rubric judges every record it gives without throwing.
verdicts.measured: 2000 garbage inputs: the importer threw 0 times; unreadable lines counted right in 2000; judged without throwing 2000

verdicts.claim: The command line: acg import --harness gemini <session.jsonl> --out F writes a record whose harness is gemini-cli and whose tool uses are the session's, by name and in order; acg judge F judges it, and P1 fails.
verdicts.measured: acg import --harness gemini wrote a record: yes, of the gemini-cli harness: yes, its tool uses the session’s in order: yes; acg judge judged it: yes, P1 failed: yes
